title: Constructive CLM-004 — Model-Level Multi-Cell Computation
scientific_question: Can learned route-addressed Cell operators perform sparse model-level simultaneous and order-sensitive sequential computation on unseen compositions while preserving a replay-free protected-mutation invariant?
new_integration_variable: multiple active learned Cells in one forward execution
operator-valued Cell state acting on hidden representations
protected mutation measured at full-composition output
not_retesting: whether replay-free certificates work in isolation
whether long-horizon Cell count tracks reusable structure

world.operator_type: learned linear residual operator g_i(h)=W_i h

operator_acquisition.learner_state: Cell-local X^T X and Y^T X sufficient statistics; no raw examples retained

evaluation.sequential_rule: h <- h + W_i h in routed order
evaluation.simultaneous_rule: h <- h + sum_i W_i h from the same incoming state

protected_mutation_probe.certificate: Core-005 row-span certificate built from current committed incoming states then raw states discarded

controls.single_cell: execute only the first routed Cell
controls.wrong_semantics: use simultaneous execution for sequential target or sequential execution for simultaneous target
controls.dense_all_cells: execute every Cell regardless of route
controls.unsafe_mutation: fit the same mutation without the Cell-local certificate

interpretation_boundary: Positive evidence is for the registered controlled linear-residual operator world.
The test promotes Cell from memory/write atom to reusable hidden-state computational module.
It does not establish nonlinear Transformer Cell operators, natural-language generation, learned router creation inside G4, learned growth control, or endogenous architecture.
Routing-search cost is not claimed to be O(active Cells); the sparse-compute gate measures expensive Cell-operator execution only.
next_if_positive: Constructive CLM-005 — Scaffold Removal / Endogenous Transition
